scope: Focused independent human mathematical and literal-source review of HPT3–HPT9 after the three requested clarifications/corrections. Later HPT10–18 are outside this focused report.
findings: HPT3 gives the exact original locally algebraic/ordinary-character dictionary, including inverse finite part, the specified Artin map, and density extending equality without topology transported through iota.
HPT4 correctly uses compact l-adic norm one and strict ordered integer weights to exclude equality and both norm twists. The exact epsilon Artin factor and the sign h_j−h_i−1 are correct.

HPT5 now explicitly starts with de Rhamness supplied by DRat. Flag subobjects and quotients inherit de Rhamness; retained exact strict period functors give additive jumps and the upper-triangular Weil polynomial at every original bridge. It does not infer de Rhamness merely from de Rham graded characters.

HPT6 preserves full IsRecT scope, rank-one character multiplicities and the original algNorm shift (1−n)/2. Under HPT4 the characters are distinct and exclude twists ±1, so the exact totally-disjoint input is applicable.

HPT7 correction verified: repeated singleton support characters are handled by the original GenericUnlinkedGL decomposition, not the stricter totally-disjoint theorem. The strict window forces segment length one; every parameter is toral with N=0. Trivial full inertia then makes all original inducing characters unramified, and explicit Iwasawa fixed vectors prove reverse sphericity.

HPT8 uses the same supplied continuous rho, full AutCsdA witness and actual flag. GUA12 and HED8 at t=(1−n)/2 give the needed attachment before semisimple comparison. Constant intertwining over a finite coefficient extension transports all period bridges. Flag transport at every prolongation exactly supplies Unl1 before WitA, and only the toral zero-monodromy RowT branch is used.

HPT9 promotes cofinite split comparison to a global polynomial identity using HED6/7, then recovers a cofinite all-place Satake identity. Original Jacquet–Shalika rigidity applied to the actual norm-twisted cusp family has the correct q^(k−(d−1)/2) sign, and positive lengths force exactly one singleton. Thus all split local components and infinity characters match, not arbitrary unitary automorphic representations.
corrections_resolved: HPT7 initially invoked totally-disjoint induction despite allowing equal characters; replaced by generic unlinked segment classification, which permits identical singleton segments.
HPT5 explicitly distinguishes de Rhamness of the supplied DRat representation from an unsupported assertion about arbitrary extensions.
HPT8 now names the precise spherical-to-Frobenius attachment consumer and its half-shift; punctuation typos corrected.
limitations: Original RowT, local classification/correspondence, period exactness, DescWeak and Jacquet–Shalika foundations remain retained as explicitly stated.
No Lean replay and no claim that this focused review alone proves RH or GRH.
